new_issues.title: collecting_firing_finished_at builds the firing time with .replace() on a session close that psycopg returns in the Denver zone, so 04:05 is read as local time.
new_issues.why: At head the function does `close.replace(hour=firing.hour, ...)` on session_close_utc with no astimezone(UTC), and the diff's own new comment says psycopg returns timestamptz in America/Denver in production, so a 20:00 UTC close (14:00 MDT) resolves to next-day 04:05 MDT plus 3 h, not 07:05 UTC. The claim is right, but the .replace() body is unchanged in base..head; the diff only changed the firing constant, the docstring and the label formatting, and the same zone error applied to the old 01:05 firing.

new_issues.title: judge_chunk_by_sessions counts any in-session bar with a valid timestamp, even one _bar_to_row will drop for bad prices.
new_issues.why: True that sessions_without_bars uses only bar_timestamp, while _bar_to_row skips bars with non-finite or non-positive OHLC, so a session holding only a bad-price bar would read as collected. The classifier this replaces (latest raw bar's date) had the same exposure, and an in-session response consisting only of unusable-price bars is a speculative provider input; hardening, not a demonstrated defect.

new_issues.title: With the trailing-weekend tolerance removed, a chunk that spans no session keeps the classifier's PARTIAL, so such a row climbs to RETRY_EXHAUSTED instead of being deleted.
new_issues.why: Mechanically true at head: the diff deleted the `days <= 4` override, judge_chunk_by_sessions returns the classifier verdict when no session closes inside the chunk, and _advance_minute_gap bumps attempt_count on PARTIAL; this contradicts the new comment that a weekend tail is SUCCESS. Chunks are up to 120 days and new gap ends are session-close aligned, so only legacy midnight-anchored actionable rows that span nothing but non-trading time reach it, and the repair only counts those rows. Settled by counting actionable minute data_gaps rows whose [gap_start, gap_end] contains no trading_sessions close in production.
